mainTopic: שמואל הקטן and ברכת המינים, the sources for the number of ברכות, the abbreviated prayer הביננו, and forgetting the rain request or הבדלה
overview: This amud finishes the story of שמואל הקטן, who forgot ברכת המינים while leading the prayers and was still not removed. The גמרא asks why, since רב rules that such a leader is removed because he may be a מין. After a debate between אביי and רבא about whether a righteous person can turn wicked, using the case of יוחנן כהן גדול, the גמרא answers that שמואל הקטן had already begun the blessing. The גמרא then explains what the seven ברכות of שבת, the nine of ראש השנה, and the twenty-four of a fast day correspond to. Next it explains רבי יהושע's abbreviated שמונה עשרה: רב says to shorten each ברכה, and שמואל gives the text of הביננו. The גמרא discusses when הביננו may not be used: after שבת and ימים טובים because of הבדלה, and in the rainy season because of the request for rain. This leads into רב אסי's ruling on who must repeat the עמידה after forgetting rain or הבדלה. A ברייתא challenges that ruling, and the answer about when the person remembers continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל הקטן tries to remember and is not removed
steps.stepSummary: The end of the story: שמואל הקטן spent two or three hours trying to remember ברכת המינים, and the people did not remove him as leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he tried hard to recall it for two or three hours, and they did not remove him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that began on the previous amud. שמואל הקטן forgot ברכת המינים while leading prayers, tried for hours to remember it, and was not removed. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key fact is that the people left him in his place, even though he could not say ברכת המינים. This fact will clash with a ruling of רב, which the גמרא brings next.

keyTerms.meaning: Looked carefully, scrutinized (here: thought hard to remember the blessing)
They brought him up, meaning they removed him from leading the prayers

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'הֶעֱלוּהוּ' as 'they promoted him.' In those days the שליח ציבור stood in a lower spot in front of the ark. Bringing him 'up' from there meant taking him out of the role.

phrases.english: And he scrutinized it (tried to recall the blessing)
phrases.notes: Refers to ברכת המינים, which he had forgotten (story begins on the previous daf).

phrases.english: for two or three hours,
and they did not remove him.
phrases.notes: They did not remove him from leading the prayers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of שמואל הקטן from the end of the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, שמואל הקטן was not removed as leader even though he forgot ברכת המינים.

steps.title: רב rules that one who skips ברכת המינים is removed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why they did not remove שמואל הקטן, since רב rules that a leader who errs in ברכת המינים is removed because we suspect he is a מין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they not remove him? Didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב: if he made a mistake in any of the blessings, we do not remove him, but in ברכת המינים we do remove him, because we suspect he may be a heretic?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. A known ruling of רב says that a leader who skips ברכת המינים must be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a mistake in prayer is just a mistake, and the leader keeps his place. ברכת המינים is different because it curses heretics, so skipping it may be on purpose: a heretic would not want to curse himself. If that is the rule, why was שמואל הקטן left in place?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] say? (introduces a contradicting source)
The blessing against heretics in שמונה עשרה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical halacha: a שליח ציבור who skips ברכת המינים is removed, while a mistake in other blessings is not a reason to remove him.

phrases.english: Why did they not remove him?
But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Rav said:
If he erred in any of the blessings, all of them —
they do not remove him,
in the blessing of the heretics — they remove him.
We suspect that perhaps he is a heretic.
phrases.notes: This is the reason for רב's ruling. The question mark in the printed text reflects the challenge as a whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי לֹא הֶעֱלוּהוּ? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the outcome of the story using a ruling of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that שמואל הקטן was not removed after failing to say ברכת המינים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that anyone who errs in ברכת המינים is removed out of suspicion of heresy. The story seems to contradict that rule.

steps.title: שמואל הקטן is different because he wrote the blessing
steps.stepSummary: There is no suspicion about שמואל הקטן, because he himself composed ברכת המינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל הקטן is different, because he is the one who composed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The man who wrote the blessing against heretics cannot be suspected of being a heretic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule rests on a suspicion that the leader skipped the blessing on purpose. With the blessing's own author, that suspicion makes no sense, so his mistake is treated as a simple lapse of memory. The rule still stands; it simply does not apply to him.

phrases.english: Shmuel HaKatan is different
because he himself instituted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a special exception to the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rule applies to every leader, so שמואל הקטן should have been removed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is based on suspicion. That suspicion does not exist for the author of the blessing, so he is not removed.

steps.title: Perhaps he changed his views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if he was righteous when he composed the blessing, maybe he later changed and became a heretic.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us be concerned that perhaps he changed his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Writing the blessing proves who he was then, but not who he is now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 3 relied on his past. The new challenge points out that people can change, so the suspicion behind רב's rule could come back.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back on it, changed his mind

phrases.english: But let us suspect that perhaps he reconsidered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the author of the blessing cannot be suspected.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being righteous in the past does not guarantee being righteous now, so the suspicion should still apply.

steps.title: אביי: a good person does not become bad
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a tradition that a truly good person does not turn wicked, so there is no need to suspect שמואל הקטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that a good person does not become bad.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the last challenge with a received tradition. A truly righteous person does not turn wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tradition removes the worry that שמואל הקטן changed. Because he was known to be righteous, the suspicion behind רב's rule does not apply to him, and the story fits the halacha.
steps.whatToRemember: A leader who errs in most blessings is not removed. A leader who skips ברכת המינים is removed because he may be a מין. אביי explains why שמואל הקטן was an exception: he wrote the blessing, and by tradition a good person does not turn bad. The גמרא tests this tradition in the next steps. According to רבא it does not hold, and step 14 gives a different answer: he had already begun the blessing.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We learned by tradition,
a good person does not become bad.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: גְּמִירִי, טָבָא לָא הָוֵי בִּישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A received tradition that removes the basis for the suspicion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since people can change, even the author of the blessing might have become a heretic.
steps.terutzMaskana: By tradition, a truly righteous person does not become wicked, so there is no suspicion about שמואל הקטן.

steps.title: A verse describes a righteous person turning away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי’s claim with a verse about a righteous person who turns from righteousness and does wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does that not happen? But isn’t it written: “When a righteous person turns from his righteousness and does wrong”?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a verse against אביי’s answer. The verse appears to say that a righteous person can change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had said that a truly good person does not turn wicked. The verse seems to describe exactly such a change.

phrases.english: And not so?! But isn’t it written:
“And when a righteous person turns from his righteousness
and does wrong.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי’s rule using a verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי’s tradition that a good person does not become bad (טבא לא הוי בישא).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse speaks of a righteous person turning away from righteousness.

steps.title: The verse describes someone who began wicked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the verse to someone who was wicked at the outset, leaving אביי’s claim about someone righteous from the outset in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: That person was wicked from the outset. But someone righteous from the outset—no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing whom the verse describes. It says the verse does not address someone who was righteous from the outset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the person in the verse became righteous after beginning wicked and then turned back. That does not yet disprove אביי’s claim about someone who began righteous.

phrases.english: That person was wicked from the outset,
but someone righteous from the outset—no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the verse so it does not contradict אביי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse concerns anyone described as righteous.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here the verse concerns someone wicked from the outset, not someone righteous from the outset.

steps.title: A משנה warns that even a longtime כהן גדול can change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה about יוחנן כהן גדול, who served for eighty years but eventually became a צדוקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is that not possible? Didn’t we learn: Do not trust yourself until the day you die. After all, יוחנן כהן גדול served in the כהונה גדולה for eighty years and eventually became a צדוקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the distinction just made. A משנה presents יוחנן כהן גדול as someone who changed after many years of service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Long service appears to make יוחנן a strong example of someone righteous who later changed. The גמרא now needs to ask whether he was righteous from the outset—the precise point of אביי’s claim.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn’t we learn in a משנה?
do not be sure of yourself

phrases.english: And not so?! But didn’t we learn:

phrases.aramaic: אַל תַּאֲמִין בְּעַצְמְךָ עַד יוֹם מוֹתְךָ,
phrases.english: Do not be sure of yourself until the day you die,
for Yoḥanan the High Priest served
in the high priesthood for eighty years
and in the end became a Sadducee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the distinction against the case of יוחנן כהן גדול.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that someone righteous from the outset cannot later become wicked.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says יוחנן כהן גדול eventually became a צדוקי despite eighty years of service.

steps.title: אביי identifies יוחנן with ינאי
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that ינאי and יוחנן are the same person, offering a way to avoid treating יוחנן as righteous from the outset.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He is ינאי; he is יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי responds by identifying the two names as one person. This is his way of answering the challenge from יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not dispute that יוחנן eventually became a צדוקי. He disputes using this case to prove that someone righteous from the outset changed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הוּא יַנַּאי, הוּא יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: Abaye said: He is Yannai; he is Yoḥanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הוּא יַנַּאי, הוּא יוֹחָנָן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by identifying יוחנן with ינאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the person in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יוחנן supplies an independent example of someone righteous from the outset who changed.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to אביי, יוחנן is ינאי, so the case need not be such an example.

steps.title: רבא distinguishes ינאי from יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבא says they are separate people: ינאי was wicked from the outset, while יוחנן was righteous from the outset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: ינאי is separate and יוחנן is separate. ינאי was wicked from the outset, and יוחנן was righteous from the outset.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different account of the two people. His account makes יוחנן’s later change a direct problem for אביי’s claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי’s answer depended on identifying יוחנן with ינאי. רבא rejects that identification and explicitly calls יוחנן righteous from the outset.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who distinguishes the two people
ינאי was wicked from the outset

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: יַנַּאי לְחוּד וְיוֹחָנָן לְחוּד,
phrases.english: Rava said: Yannai is separate and Yoḥanan is separate,
Yannai was wicked from the outset,
and Yoḥanan was righteous from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: יַנַּאי לְחוּד וְיוֹחָנָן לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי’s identification and offers a different account.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ינאי and יוחנן are distinct; יוחנן was righteous from the outset.

steps.title: רבא’s account leaves the challenge in place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says אביי’s account works, but רבא’s account is difficult because יוחנן began righteous and later changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works according to אביי, but according to רבא it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two accounts. It points out that רבא’s account still conflicts with the claim that someone righteous from the outset cannot change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, יוחנן can be treated as someone who did not begin righteous. For רבא, יוחנן did begin righteous, yet the משנה says he became a צדוקי.

phrases.english: This works according to Abaye,
but according to Rava it is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the problem created by רבא’s distinction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא’s account of יוחנן alongside the earlier claim about someone righteous from the outset.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא calls יוחנן righteous from the outset, while the משנה says יוחנן later became a צדוקי.

steps.title: רבא allows that a righteous person might change
steps.stepSummary: רבא can answer that even someone righteous from the outset might later change.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could say to you: Even someone righteous from the outset might perhaps change his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבא’s answer to the difficulty. רבא does not accept אביי’s firm rule about someone righteous from the outset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On רבא’s view, יוחנן’s later change is possible even though he began righteous. But this also removes the earlier reason for dismissing suspicion about שמואל הקטן.

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: צַדִּיק מֵעִיקָּרוֹ נָמֵי דִּלְמָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Even someone righteous from the outset might perhaps change his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty for רבא but reopens the earlier issue about שמואל הקטן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumed rule that initial righteousness rules out later change.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Someone righteous from the outset cannot later change.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even someone righteous from the outset might later change.

steps.title: Why was שמואל הקטן not removed?
steps.stepSummary: If even someone righteous from the outset might change, the גמרא returns to its original question about שמואל הקטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why did they not remove him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier question about שמואל הקטן. If a righteous person might change, why did they leave him as leader?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי’s answer had protected שמואל הקטן from suspicion because he had composed ברכת המינים. רבא’s position means his earlier righteousness cannot, by itself, settle the concern.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא’s view brings the discussion back to why שמואל הקטן was not removed. The next step answers this: he had already begun the ברכה.

phrases.english: If so, why did they not remove him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא’s answer back to the unresolved concern about שמואל הקטן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision not to remove שמואל הקטן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If someone righteous from the outset might later change, composing ברכת המינים earlier does not by itself rule out later suspicion.

steps.title: Beginning the blessing makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הקטן had already begun the ברכה. A teaching explains why that matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל הקטן is different because he began the blessing. רב יהודה said in the name of רב—or, according to another attribution, רבי יהושע בן לוי—that the rule applies only when the person did not begin it. If he began it, he finishes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about שמואל הקטן. It supports the answer with a rule about someone who begins the ברכה but then gets stuck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not beginning the ברכה raises a concern about the person leading the prayer. שמואל הקטן had begun it, so his difficulty finishing does not create that same concern.

keyTerms.meaning: when he did not begin it

phrases.english: Shmuel HaKatan is different, because he began it.
For Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and some say it was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הִתְחִיל בָּהּ,
phrases.english: They taught this only when he did not begin it,
but if he began it, he finishes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the renewed question about שמואל הקטן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes beginning the ברכה from not beginning it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a person might change, שמואל הקטן should also have been suspect.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because שמואל הקטן began the ברכה, he could finish it.

steps.title: Why are there seven blessings on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new line of questions about the numbers of ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: These seven blessings of שבת—what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the seven ברכות of שבת and asks what their number corresponds to. This question sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion concerned a problem during a ברכה. The new discussion asks why a תפילה contains a particular number of ברכות.

phrases.english: These seven of Shabbat—what do they correspond to?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new discussion after the answer about שמואל הקטן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the seven שבת ברכות correspond to.

steps.title: The seven blessings correspond to seven voices
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלפתא בן שאול connects the number seven to seven קולות spoken by דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלפתא בן שאול said: They correspond to the seven “voices” that דוד spoke of over the waters.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלפתא בן שאול answers the question about the seven ברכות of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer gives another place where the number seven appears. It connects the number of ברכות to seven קולות in דוד’s words.

phrases.english: Rabbi Halafta ben Shaul said:
Corresponding to seven “voices”
that David spoke of over the waters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the number seven.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seven שבת ברכות correspond to seven קולות spoken of by דוד.

steps.title: Why are there nine blessings on ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the nine ברכות of ראש השנה correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: These nine blessings of ראש השנה—what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the type of question, now about nine ברכות of ראש השנה. It is setting up another numerical connection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The subject changes from שבת to ראש השנה. The question still seeks a source matching the number of ברכות.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי תֵּשַׁע דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כְּנֶגֶד מִי?
phrases.english: These nine of Rosh Hashanah—what do they correspond to?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תֵּשַׁע דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of question to ראש השנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the nine ראש השנה ברכות correspond to.

steps.title: Nine mentions in חנה’s prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק דמן קרטיגנין points to nine mentions in חנה’s prayer, then explains its connection to ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק דמן קרטיגנין said: They correspond to nine mentions of God in חנה’s prayer. As the Master said: On ראש השנה, שרה, רחל, and חנה were remembered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק דמן קרטיגנין answers with חנה’s prayer. The גמרא then supplies a reason to connect חנה to ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nine אזכרות explain the number nine. The statement that חנה was remembered on ראש השנה explains why her prayer is relevant here.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzhak of Kartignin said:
Corresponding to nine mentions of God
that Hannah said in her prayer,
as the Master said:
On Rosh Hashanah were remembered
Sarah, Rachel, and Hannah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about nine and explains the ראש השנה connection.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nine ברכות correspond to nine אזכרות in חנה’s prayer.

steps.title: Why are there twenty-four blessings on fast days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the twenty-four ברכות of a fast-day תפילה correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: These twenty-four blessings of a fast day—what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the number of ברכות on fast days. This sets up a third numerical connection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question follows the same pattern as the questions about שבת and ראש השנה. This time, the number needing explanation is twenty-four.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע דְּתַעֲנִיתָא כְּנֶגֶד מִי?
phrases.english: These twenty-four of a fast day—what do they correspond to?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע דְּתַעֲנִיתָא כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ראש השנה to fast-day תפילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the twenty-four fast-day ברכות correspond to.

steps.title: Twenty-four songs when the ark was brought in
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו connects the twenty-four ברכות to twenty-four רננות said by שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said: They correspond to twenty-four “songs” that שלמה said when he brought the ארון into the בית קדשי הקדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלבו gives a match for the number twenty-four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה said twenty-four רננות when he brought the ארון into the בית קדשי הקדשים. The answer matches the number, but by itself it does not explain why those ברכות belong specifically on fast days. Step 22 explains that.

phrases.english: Rabbi Helbo said:
Corresponding to twenty-four “songs”
that Solomon said at the time
when he brought the ark into the Holy of Holies:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what the number twenty-four matches.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It corresponds to twenty-four רננות said by שלמה.

steps.title: Why not say them every day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges whether a numerical match explains why these ברכות are limited to fast days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us say them every day as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חלבו’s answer. If the twenty-four רננות are the reason, why not say twenty-four ברכות every day?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source explains the number twenty-four, but it does not yet explain the choice of day. The challenge asks for that missing connection.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, כׇּל יוֹמָא נָמֵי נֵמְרִינְהוּ!
phrases.english: If so, let us say them every day as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כׇּל יוֹמָא נָמֵי נֵמְרִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the fast-day limit in רבי חלבו’s answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The connection between שלמה’s twenty-four רננות and fast-day ברכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A match in number alone does not explain why the ברכות are not said every day.

steps.title: They belong to a day of seeking mercy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why שלמה’s רננות fit fast days rather than every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did שלמה say them? On a day of seeking mercy. We, too, say them on a day of seeking mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by identifying the kind of day on which שלמה spoke. It then compares that day to a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link is not just the number twenty-four. שלמה said the רננות on a day of seeking mercy, and the extra ברכות are likewise said on a day of seeking mercy.

keyTerms.meaning: on a day of seeking mercy

steps.whatToRemember: The twenty-four רננות explain both the number of ברכות and, because they were said on a day of seeking mercy, why the extra ברכות fit a fast day.

phrases.english: When did Solomon say them?
On a day of seeking mercy.
We, too, on a day of seeking mercy
say them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the day-specific connection that the challenge requested.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Matches the occasion, not only the number.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The twenty-four רננות could support saying twenty-four ברכות every day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their connection to a day of seeking mercy supports saying the extra ברכות on a fast day.

steps.title: רבי יהושע calls for an abbreviated prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says to recite an abbreviated שמונה עשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: An abbreviated eighteen-blessing prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי יהושע’s wording from the משנה. This sets up a question about what “abbreviated” means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement calls for a shorter תפילה but does not yet give its wording. The next step asks how to make it shorter.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage whose view is being explained

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
An abbreviated eighteen-blessing prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of fast-day blessings, the גמרא turns to רבי יהושע’s wording about the daily תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע calls for an abbreviated שמונה עשרה.

steps.title: What does the abbreviated prayer mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהושע means by an abbreviated שמונה עשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is an abbreviated eighteen-blessing prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical meaning of רבי יהושע’s phrase. It is preparing for two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The open point is whether each ברכה is shortened or several ברכות are replaced by one shorter text.

phrases.english: What is an abbreviated eighteen-blessing prayer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks how to understand the wording just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What form of abbreviated תפילה does רבי יהושע require?

steps.title: Shorten each blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב says to give an abbreviated version of every ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: An abbreviated version of each and every blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: shorten each ברכה individually.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the abbreviation is spread across the תפילה. רב has not supplied a single replacement text.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage giving the first answer

phrases.english: Rav said:
An abbreviated version of each and every blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב answers the question with one way to shorten the תפילה.

steps.title: Say the combined prayer הביננו
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives the text of הביננו, one short ברכה that brings together the requests of the middle ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Grant us understanding, Lord our God, to know Your ways; turn our hearts toward reverence for You; forgive us so that we may be redeemed; keep us far from suffering; nourish us in the pastures of Your land; gather our scattered people from the four directions; judge those who stray according to Your will; raise Your hand against the wicked; let the righteous rejoice in the rebuilding of Your city and the restoration of Your Sanctuary, in the flourishing of דוד Your servant and the preparation of a light for the משיח, son of ישי. Before we call, answer us. Blessed are You, Lord, Who hears prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different answer by quoting the text of הביננו. It combines many requests in one ברכה rather than shortening each middle ברכה separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the text recalls a request from the regular middle ברכות. The prayer ends with the closing words of שומע תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage giving the second answer
grant us understanding; the opening word of this short prayer

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Grant us understanding, Lord our God, to know Your ways,
and turn our hearts toward reverence for You,
and forgive us so that we may be redeemed,
and keep us far from our suffering,
and nourish us in the pastures of Your land,
and gather our scattered people from the four directions,
and let those who stray be judged according to Your will,
and raise Your hand against the wicked,
and may the righteous rejoice in the rebuilding of Your city
and in the restoration of Your Sanctuary,
and in the flourishing of the royal line of David Your servant
and in the preparation of a light for the Messiah, son of Yishai,
before we call, may You answer.
Blessed are You, Lord, Who hears prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל offers a different form of abbreviation from רב’s.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Recite the combined text of הביננו in place of the separate middle ברכות.

steps.title: אביי objects to reciting הביננו
steps.stepSummary: אביי sharply disapproves of someone who prays הביננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי would curse someone who prayed הביננו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds אביי’s sharp objection to reciting הביננו. It does not explain his reason here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל has just provided a valid shortened text, but אביי objects to its use. This line does not spell out exactly when אביי would allow it.

phrases.english: Abaye would curse over it
someone who prayed ‘Grant us understanding.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי reacts to the prayer text שמואל just gave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי sharply objects to reciting הביננו.

steps.title: A restriction after שבת and ימים טובים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes שמואל: הביננו may be said during the year, except after שבת and ימים טובים, when הבדלה must be said in חונן הדעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said that שמואל said: Throughout the year a person prays הביננו, except at the conclusion of שבת and at the conclusion of ימים טובים, because one must say הבדלה in חונן הדעת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן quotes שמואל giving a specific exception to reciting הביננו. The issue is where to place הבדלה in the evening תפילה after שבת or a יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הבדלה belongs in חונן הדעת, but הביננו does not give that ברכה its usual separate place. That creates a problem on those evenings.

keyTerms.meaning: the declaration separating a holy day from an ordinary day
the blessing about God granting knowledge

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Shmuel said:
Throughout the entire year, a person prays Havineinu,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִמּוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת וּמִמּוֹצָאֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים,
phrases.english: except at the conclusion of Shabbat and at the conclusion of festivals,
because one must say havdala
in ‘Who grants knowledge.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי’s objection, the גמרא states a particular time when שמואל says not to use הביננו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not recite הביננו after שבת or ימים טובים, because הבדלה must be said in חונן הדעת.

steps.title: Why not give הבדלה its own blessing?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל challenges the exception: say הבדלה as a separate fourth ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל objects: Let us say it as a fourth blessing on its own!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שמואל challenges the reason for excluding הביננו. He suggests putting הבדלה in its own fourth ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הבדלה can have a separate place, its absence from the usual חונן הדעת would not prevent someone from reciting הביננו. The next step brings support for that option.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel strongly objects:
Let us say it as a fourth blessing on its own!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It attacks the reason given for the exception after שבת and ימים טובים.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל’s exclusion of הביננו when הבדלה must be recited.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A separate fourth ברכה could make room for הבדלה without requiring the usual separate חונן הדעת.

steps.title: A משנה allows a separate fourth blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל cites a משנה: רבי עקיבא places הבדלה in its own fourth ברכה, while רבי אליעזר places it in הודאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did we not learn: רבי עקיבא says, ‘One says it as a fourth blessing on its own.’ רבי אליעזר says, ‘In the blessing of thanksgiving (הודאה).’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supplies support for רבה בר שמואל’s challenge from a משנה. The cited משנה records more than one place for הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא explicitly allows the separate fourth ברכה that רבה בר שמואל suggested. רבי אליעזר gives a different location, הודאה. The next step answers the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: did we not learn in a משנה?
the sage who places it in a separate fourth blessing
the sage who gives a different placement

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא תְּנַן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Did we not learn: Rabbi Akiva says:
One says it as a fourth blessing on its own.
Rabbi Eliezer says: In the blessing of thanksgiving.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא תְּנַן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It backs up the proposed separate ברכה with an explicit view in a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The proposal to say הבדלה as its own fourth ברכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in which רבי עקיבא says to recite it as a separate fourth ברכה.

steps.title: A separate blessing would add one too many
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proposal to give הבדלה its own blessing after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we follow רבי עקיבא all year, so that we should follow him now? We do not: eighteen blessings were instituted, not nineteen. Here too, seven were instituted, not eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proposal from the previous step. It says that the option found in רבי עקיבא’s view does not fit the established number of blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A separate הבדלה blessing would add a blessing. The גמרא compares this to the ordinary year, when it does not add a nineteenth blessing to follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Why, throughout the entire year,
do we act according to Rabbi Akiva,
that we should do so now too?!
Throughout the entire year, what is the reason
we do not act according to Rabbi Akiva?
They instituted eighteen,
not nineteen.
Here too, they instituted seven,
not eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ מִי עָבְדִינַן כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed use of רבי עקיבא’s separate fourth blessing.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Adding a separate הבדלה blessing in this setting.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would increase the established number of blessings from seven to eight.

steps.title: Why not include the distinction within הביננו?
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא proposes putting הבדלה into the existing text of הביננו; the גמרא leaves this challenge difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא objects: Why not include it in the abridged text: ‘Grant us understanding, Lord our God, Who distinguishes between sacred and ordinary’? This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges the last answer. Instead of adding a blessing, he suggests adding הבדלה to the blessing already being said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seven-versus-eight answer rules out a separate blessing. It does not explain why הבדלה cannot be inserted into הביננו without changing the number of blessings. The גמרא gives no answer here.

keyTerms.meaning: let us include it within the existing text

phrases.english: Mar Zutra strongly objects to this:
Let us include it within the existing text:
‘Grant us understanding, Lord our God,
Who distinguishes between sacred and ordinary’!
This remains difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ מָר זוּטְרָא: וְנִכְלְלָה מִכְלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the number-of-blessings answer addresses insertion into an existing blessing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The continuing exclusion of הביננו after שבת and ימים טובים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding words inside הביננו would include הבדלה without adding an eighth blessing.

steps.title: A new restriction during the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי says not to use הביננו during the rainy season because the request for rain belongs in ברכת השנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: A person may pray הביננו throughout the year, except during the rainy season, because one must say the request for rain in ברכת השנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new case in which הביננו is restricted. רב ביבי בר אביי points to the required request for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier problem was where to say הבדלה. This ruling raises a similar placement problem for the rain request, which belongs in ברכת השנים.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
Throughout the year, a person may pray ‘Grant us understanding,’
except during the rainy season,
because one must say the request
in the blessing of ‘the years.’

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי: כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ מִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם ״הֲבִינֵנוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the unresolved הבדלה objection to a different exception involving rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During ימות הגשמים, one does not use הביננו because the request for rain must be said in ברכת השנים.

steps.title: Why not add the rain request inside הביננו?
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא suggests inserting the request for dew and rain into the abridged wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא strongly objects: Why not include it in the existing text: ‘Satisfy us with the pastures of Your land, and grant dew and rain’?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges the rainy-season restriction. He proposes adding the rain request inside הביננו rather than giving up the abridged prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same kind of suggestion as his earlier הבדלה objection. The proposed words would supply the request that רב ביבי בר אביי says is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: with the pastures of Your land

phrases.english: Mar Zutra strongly objects to this:
Let us include it within the existing text:
‘And satisfy us with the pastures of Your land,
and grant dew and rain’!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ מָר זוּטְרָא: וְנִכְלְלָה מִכְלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a way to say the required request without abandoning הביננו.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי בר אביי’s exclusion of הביננו during ימות הגשמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rain request can be inserted into the abridged text, its absence need not prevent use of הביננו.

steps.title: An added phrase may cause confusion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that inserting the rain request could confuse the person praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He might become confused.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer to מר זוטרא’s rain proposal. Changing the familiar wording could cause confusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not say the rain request is unnecessary. It says that relying on a newly inserted phrase is a problem for the person reciting הביננו.

phrases.english: He might become confused.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proposed insertion of the rain request.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical difficulty in reciting modified wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One could insert the rain request into הביננו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such an insertion may confuse the person praying.

steps.title: Would the same concern apply to הבדלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests its confusion answer against the earlier proposal to insert הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, adding the distinction in ‘Who grants understanding’ might also cause confusion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer by returning to הבדלה. If inserting rain causes confusion, inserting הבדלה seems to have the same problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier הבדלה objection was left as קַשְׁיָא, without this answer. The גמרא now asks why the confusion answer was used for rain but not for הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: the distinction between sacred and ordinary
the blessing concerning the granting of understanding

phrases.english: If so,
the distinction in ‘Who grants understanding’
might also cause confusion!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the confusion answer against the earlier הבדלה case.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using possible confusion to answer the rain-insertion objection while leaving the הבדלה-insertion objection unanswered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same concern about inserted wording appears to apply to הבדלה as well.

steps.title: Beginning of the prayer versus middle of the prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that הבדלה would come at the start of הביננו, so it does not confuse the person praying. The rain request would come in the middle, so it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: There (הבדלה), since it comes at the beginning of the prayer, he will not get confused. Here (rain), since it comes in the middle of the prayer, he will get confused.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 36: why does the confusion problem apply to the rain request but not to הבדלה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: הבדלה belongs in חונן הדעת, which is the very first idea in הביננו, so the person adds it right away while his mind is still fresh. The rain request belongs in ברכת השנים, which falls in the middle of the short prayer. Stopping there to add something could throw him off.

phrases.english: They say: there, since it comes
at the beginning of the prayer, he is not confused;
phrases.notes: הבדלה goes in חונן הדעת, the first of the middle blessings.

phrases.english: here, since it comes
in the middle of the prayer, he is confused.
phrases.notes: The rain request belongs in ברכת השנים, in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם כֵּיוָן דְּאָתְיָא בִּתְחִלַּת צְלוֹתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36 by telling the two cases apart.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק) based on where in the prayer the addition falls
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If adding הבדלה does not confuse, adding rain should not confuse either.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the addition falls matters. At the start there is no confusion. In the middle there is.

steps.title: רב אשי: put the rain request in the שומע תפלה part
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks why we cannot put the rain request at the end of הביננו, in the part matching שומע תפלה, since רב אסי rules that the rain request can be said in שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: Let him say it in שומע תפלה. For רבי תנחום said in the name of רב אסי: If someone mistakenly did not mention גבורות גשמים in תחיית המתים, we send him back. If he forgot the request for rain in ברכת השנים, we do not send him back, because he can say it in שומע תפלה. If he forgot הבדלה in חונן הדעת, we do not send him back, because he can say it over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges the confusion answer. He suggests putting the rain request at the end of הביננו, where the שומע תפלה part is, so it would not interrupt the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is רב אסי's ruling: someone who forgot the rain request in ברכת השנים can make it up in שומע תפלה. So שומע תפלה is a valid place for rain. Adding it at the end of הביננו would avoid the 'middle of the prayer' confusion problem completely.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who listens to prayer,' the last of the middle blessings, where personal requests can be added
Mentioning the might of the rains (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם)
We make him go back and repeat
'Who grants knowledge,' the blessing where הבדלה (אתה חוננתנו) is added
Over the cup of wine (the regular הבדלה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up two different things. גבורות גשמים is the praise (משיב הרוח) said in the second blessing. שאלה is the actual request for rain (ותן טל ומטר) said in ברכת השנים. They have different rules.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi strongly objected to it:
Let him say it in 'Who listens to prayer,'
phrases.notes: Meaning at the end of הביננו, which matches שומע תפלה.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Tanchum said in the name of Rav Asi:
If he erred and did not mention the might of the rains
in 'revival of the dead,' we send him back.
If he forgot the request in the blessing of the years,
we do not send him back,
because he can say it in 'Who listens to prayer.'
And if he forgot havdala in 'Who grants knowledge,'
we do not send him back,
because he can say it over the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: וְנֵימְרַהּ בְּ״שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the 'middle of the prayer' concern but offers a placement that avoids it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי בר אביי's rule (step 33) that הביננו may not be used in the rainy season, and the confusion answer that supports it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שומע תפלה is a valid place for the rain request, as רב אסי rules. Putting it at the end of הביננו avoids confusion, so there is no reason to forbid הביננו in the rainy season.

steps.title: A mistake is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שומע תפלה works for the rain request only after a mistake. It is not a place to plan to say it from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who erred is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back רב אשי's suggestion. רב אסי's rule only helps someone who already made a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making up the rain request in שומע תפלה is a backup fix (בדיעבד). You may not choose it on purpose (לכתחילה). A person cannot use הביננו and plan to put rain at the end, so the ban on הביננו in the rainy season stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The rain request belongs in ברכת השנים. Saying it in שומע תפלה is only a fix after forgetting, so הביננו is not used in the rainy season.

phrases.english: One who erred is different.
phrases.notes: The backup option applies only בדיעבד, not לכתחילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי by limiting how far רב אסי's ruling reaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the proof: a בדיעבד rule does not allow a לכתחילה practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since rain may be said in שומע תפלה, one could plan to say it there in הביננו.
steps.terutzMaskana: שומע תפלה is only a fallback for someone who forgot, so it cannot be used to allow הביננו.

steps.title: Looking at רב אסי's ruling on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב אסי's ruling (quoted in passing above) to examine it directly: forgetting גבורות גשמים requires repeating the prayer, but forgetting the rain request or הבדלה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רבי תנחום said in the name of רב אסי: If someone mistakenly did not mention גבורות גשמים in תחיית המתים, we send him back. If he forgot the request in ברכת השנים, we do not send him back, because he can say it in שומע תפלה. If he forgot הבדלה in חונן הדעת, we do not send him back, because he can say it over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא now studies רב אסי's statement for its own sake. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Above, the statement was only used as a proof for רב אשי. Now it becomes the main topic. It has three rules: back for גבורות גשמים, not back for the rain request, and not back for הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': returning to examine a statement that was quoted in passing
The second blessing of the עמידה, where משיב הרוח is said
The ninth blessing, for a good year, where the rain request is said

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Tanchum said in the name of Rav Asi:
If he erred and did not mention the might of the rains
in 'revival of the dead,' we send him back.
If he forgot the request in the blessing of the years,
we do not send him back,
because he can say it in 'Who listens to prayer.'
And if he forgot havdala in 'Who grants knowledge,'
we do not send him back,
because he can say it over the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the statement quoted in step 38, now as the main subject for analysis.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forgetting גבורות גשמים requires repeating the עמידה. Forgetting the rain request (fixable in שומע תפלה) or הבדלה (fixable over the cup) does not.

steps.title: A ברייתא says forgetting the rain request does require going back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אסי from a ברייתא that agrees on גבורות גשמים and הבדלה, but rules that someone who forgot the rain request in ברכת השנים must go back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: If someone mistakenly did not mention the might of the rains in 'revival of the dead,' we send him back. If he forgot the request in the blessing of the years, we send him back. If he forgot הבדלה in 'Who grants knowledge,' we do not send him back, because he can say it over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב אסי on one rule: the rain request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of the three rules match רב אסי exactly. The difference is the middle case: רב אסי says no need to go back because of שומע תפלה, but the ברייתא says he must go back. The ברייתא also never mentions the שומע תפלה fix, which makes the contradiction sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: They objected (from a תנאי source such as a ברייתא)
The request for rain (ותן טל ומטר), as opposed to the praise of rain

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר גְּבוּרוֹת גְּשָׁמִים
phrases.english: They objected: If he erred and did not mention the might of the rains
in 'revival of the dead,' we send him back.
If he forgot the request in the blessing of the years,
we send him back,
phrases.notes: This is the point of contradiction with רב אסי.

phrases.english: and if he forgot havdala in 'Who grants knowledge,'
we do not send him back,
because he can say it over the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר גְּבוּרוֹת גְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling just restated in step 40 using an earlier, more authoritative source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling that forgetting the rain request in ברכת השנים does not require going back
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא (a תנאי source, which outranks an אמורא) rules that he must go back, which directly contradicts רב אסי.

steps.title: Splitting the cases: one praying alone versus one praying with a congregation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא, which says to go back, is about a יחיד. רב אסי, who says not to go back, is about someone praying in a ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a problem. This source is talking about an individual, and that source is talking about a congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to solve the contradiction by saying the two sources describe two different people: one praying alone and one praying with a group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's rule (go back) is for a יחיד, who has no one else to cover his mistake. רב אסי's rule (do not go back) is for someone in a ציבור. This removes the contradiction without saying that either source is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer that splits the cases.
An individual praying on his own

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this one is about an individual,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the ברייתא, which requires going back.

phrases.english: and that one is about a congregation.
phrases.notes: "That one" is רב אסי, who says he does not go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּיָחִיד, הָא בְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 41.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): individual versus congregation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי and the ברייתא seemed to rule in opposite ways on the very same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They describe different situations: the ברייתא is about a יחיד, and רב אסי is about a ציבור.

steps.title: The congregation answer does not match רב אסי's stated reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a person in a ציבור would not go back. The only reason would be that he hears the prayer from the שליח ציבור. But then רב אסי should have given that reason, not 'because he can say it in שומע תפלה'. So the answer is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a congregation, why would he not go back? Because he hears it from the prayer leader. If so, then instead of saying 'because he can say it in שומע תפלה', he should have said 'because he hears it from the prayer leader'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the last answer by asking for the real reason behind the congregation rule. It finds that this reason does not match the words רב אסי actually used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person is excused because the שליח ציבור's repetition covers him, then שומע תפלה plays no part. Yet רב אסי pointed to שומע תפלה as his reason. So רב אסי cannot have been talking about a ציבור, and the answer in step 42 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer leader, who repeats the עמידה for the congregation
If so. This introduces a problem that follows from the suggestion.
He should have said. The speaker's actual wording does not fit.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the congregation idea is false as a matter of law. It is only showing that this idea cannot explain רב אסי's words, because he gave a different reason.

phrases.english: In a congregation, what is the reason he does not go back?
Because he hears it from the prayer leader.
phrases.notes: The prayer leader's repetition covers him.

phrases.english: If so, this phrase
'because he can say it in שומע תפלה',
phrases.notes: These are רב אסי's actual words.

phrases.english: should have been 'because he hears it from the prayer leader'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַאי ״מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְאוֹמְרָהּ בְּשׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִילָּה״, ״מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשּׁוֹמֵעַ מִשְּׁלִיחַ צִיבּוּר״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the individual-versus-congregation answer from step 42.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole answer that splits the cases into יחיד and ציבור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The real reason in a congregation would be the שליח ציבור's repetition. That clashes with רב אסי's stated reason, which is שומע תפלה.

steps.title: New answer: both sources are about an individual, and timing decides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. Both sources are about a יחיד. רב אסי's 'no need to go back' applies when he remembers before reaching שומע תפלה, so he can still add the request there. The other half of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both this and that are about an individual, and it is still not a problem: this one is where he remembered before reaching 'שומע תפלה'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the congregation idea and starts a new answer based on when the person remembers his mistake. This line sets up the second half of the answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources now describe a יחיד. The difference is timing. If he remembers before שומע תפלה, he can fix the mistake there, which matches רב אסי's reason exactly. The opposite case, where he only remembers after שומע תפלה, will be matched to the ברייתא's 'go back'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This drops the previous answer and brings a new one.

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that are about an individual,
and it is still not a problem:
this one is where he remembered before reaching 'שומע תפלה',
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי's case. He can still add the rain request in שומע תפלה. The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּיָחִיד, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 43 with a new answer based on timing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by timing: remembering before or after שומע תפלה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was thought to be individual versus congregation, but that did not fit רב אסי's wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sources are about a יחיד. When he remembers before שומע תפלה, he does not go back, which is רב אסי's case. The other half of the answer follows on the next amud.
